newsitem.title: GERMANY: DB Cargo sees 1.3pct '96 intermodal freight growth.
newsitem.headline: DB Cargo sees 1.3pct '96 intermodal freight growth.

text.p: DB Cargo, the railfreight division of German Railways, said it expected intermodal freight volumes to rise 1.3 percent to 30.4 million tonnes in 1996.
In a statement DB Cargo chairman Dr Eberhard Sinnecker said the Deutsche Bahn AG (DB) division would transport 2.85 million containers and other combined freight equipment this year.
Sinnecker was speaking at the opening of a combined freight terminal of Swiss intermodal transport company Hupac in Singen, south-west Germany, on Friday, the statement said.
The new Hupac terminal would be used to operate joint trans-Alpine freight services with Swiss Railways to serve Italy, it added.
Sinnecker said DB Cargo aimed to transport 50 million tonnes of intermodal freight by 2006 and 90 million tonnes in the long-term.
German Railways already transported the equivalent of 7,600 truckloads of freight a day, he added.
To achieve this goal, Deutsche Bahn and the German government were investing several hundred million marks in expanding intermodal infrastructure in Germany, Sinnecker said.

The new Hupac terminal was one of 27 private and 54 DB Cargo terminals linked by 200 daily services of DB Cargo and other intermodal rail companies, he added. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
